questions.question: How many 15-minute real-time intervals at ERCOT's West hub (HB_WEST) settled above 100 USD per MWh in the week of Monday 26 October to Sunday 1 November 2026 (Central time)?
questions.answer:
I could not get an exact count. The data is in the warehouse, but the tools cannot count rows above a price threshold, and I ran out of calls before I could pin it down. HB_WEST has 676 fifteen-minute spp_rtm intervals for 26 Oct to 1 Nov 2026 in Central time (iso_rtm_hub_prices, source table). All times below are Central (America/Chicago). What the table does show:
- Highest interval of the week: 209.55 USD/MWh, at 2026-11-01T02:45Z, which is 21:45 on 31 Oct local.
- Only 26 Oct and 31 Oct reach above 100 USD/MWh. The daily maxima are 121.52 on 26 Oct and 209.55 on 31 Oct. The other days peak below 100: 72.04, 63.63, 47.77, 47.23 and 68.61 USD/MWh (27 Oct to 1 Nov).
- 26 Oct: only the top few intervals of the day exceed 100. A rank-based percentile cut near the top of that day's values is already 93.67 USD/MWh, below 100.
- 31 Oct: many intervals exceed 100. A percentile cut well down the day's sorted values is still 108.62 USD/MWh. Every interval in the 21:00 hour (minimum 158.52) and the 22:00 hour (minimum 104.63) is above 100. The 23:00 hour is mixed (minimum 67.40, maximum 167.07). The 08:00, 09:00, 16:00, 17:00 and 20:00 hours also have maxima above 100 but minima below it, so they are mixed too.
The exact count of intervals above 100 USD/MWh is therefore not determined by what I could read, and I will not estimate it.
